topic: The Infinite in a Finite Box: An Introduction to Space-Filling Curves
target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: The Dimensional Paradox (Prerequisites)
lecture_lines: A 1D line has length, no area.
A 2D square has area, infinite points.
Can a 1D line visit every 2D point?
animations: 1. Display text 'Dimensional Paradox' in center with color #FFFFFF.
2. Fade in small circles representing points, color #FF5733.
3. Highlight gaps between points with glowing color #33FF57.
4. Transform circles into a line, color #3357FF.

sections.title: The Peano Construction (Iterative Logic)
lecture_lines: Iterative fractals start with a simple generator.
We replace segments with a new shape repeatedly.
Each step fills more of the square.
animations: 3. Iteratively build sequence: 0, S(0), S(S(0)), color #00FFCC.

sections.title: Crossing the Finite-Infinite Bridge
lecture_lines: Finite steps are just simple line segments.
animations: 1. Show finite set of objects, color #FFFFFF.
3. Show bijection between finite and infinite, color #FFFF33.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Hilbert Curve
lecture_lines: They preserve spatial locality in memory.
Useful for image compression and processing.
animations: 2. Draw Hilbert curve starting from center, color #00CCFF.
3. Increase recursive depth, curve fills square, color #00FF33.

sections.title: Conclusion: Reconciling Intuition
lecture_lines: Infinite curves are powerful design tools.
They solve complex optimization problems efficiently.
animations: 1. Show paradox and logic side-by-side, color #FFFFFF.
2. Overlay them to form cohesive theory, color #FF6600.
3. Fade to final summary text, color #FFFFFF.
